title: Performing Foundations: Solo, Ensemble & Stage Craft
welcome_lead: Step onto the stage and master the basics of performing — from solo recitals to ensemble teamwork.
meta_desc: GCSE Music Performing Adventure 1: foundations of solo and ensemble performance, accuracy, expression and stage technique.
final_note: You have the foundations of a confident performer — take a bow!

walkthroughs.body_html:
For GCSE you usually submit a solo and an ensemble performance. A solo lets you shine individually, with all attention on your tone, accuracy and expression. An ensemble tests your ability to listen, blend and stay in time with others.

In an ensemble your part may be less exposed, but you must lock in with the group's pulse, balance your volume and follow visual cues from a leader or conductor.

Examiners reward accuracy (right notes and rhythms), fluency (no hesitations) and expression (dynamics, phrasing, articulation).

Choosing a piece at the right difficulty is crucial — a simple piece played beautifully often beats a hard piece played roughly. Practise slowly with a metronome, then build speed.

Good performers prepare mentally as well as musically. Warm up, breathe, and visualise a confident start. Walk on, acknowledge the audience, settle, then begin.

If you slip, don't stop — keep the pulse going. Examiners value musical continuity over panicked restarts.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes Classical (1750-1820) from Baroque style?
options: Classical means any old serious music.
Clearer melodic phrases, homophonic texture, balanced structures like sonata form.
Use of orchestra (Baroque had none).
A cadence using only major chords.

mcqs.q: What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: Classical means any old serious music.
A piece six bars long.
Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
A cadence using only major chords.
Classical means any old serious music.
A cadence ending on chord V, creating a sense of incompleteness.
A cadence that sounds wrong or is performed badly.
